### 1.1-1.3 Problem Analysis

The issue is about improving the default color behavior in the reportseff tool:

**Current Problem**: When output exceeds 20 lines, the tool uses `click.echo_via_pager()` with `color=True` by default, causing ANSI escape codes to appear in both terminal output and piped files, making the output garbled.

**Desired Solution**: Change the default behavior to use Click's automatic color detection, so:
- Terminal output shows colors appropriately
- Piped output to files doesn't include ANSI codes
- Explicit `--color`/`--no-color` flags continue to work

### 1.4 Steps to Reproduce
1. Run `reportseff --since d=7` with >20 job entries
2. Observe ANSI escape codes in output
3. Pipe output to file: `reportseff --since d=7 > output_file`
4. See ANSI codes in the file

### 1.5 Best Practices
- Preserve existing CLI flag functionality
- Make minimal changes to core logic
- Ensure backward compatibility
- Test both pager and non-pager scenarios

     5	# `reportseff`
     6	
     7	> A python script for tabular display of slurm efficiency information
     8	
     9	![Example](https://github.com/troycomi/reportseff/raw/main/imgs/example.png)
    10	
    11	## About
    12	
    13	### Motivation
    14	
    15	Whether a sys admin or cluster user, knowing how well you are estimating job
    16	resources can help streamline job scheduling and maximize your priority. If you
    17	have ever tried to use `sacct` you probably had some trouble interpreting the
    18	output.  While `seff` or `jobstats` can provide detailed summaries, they don't
    19	scale easily to array jobs or offer a way to see all the jobs from a single
    20	user.  `reportseff` aims to fill this role.  Read more about the [motivation
    21	for reportseff](https://github.com/troycomi/reportseff/blob/main/ABOUT.md).
    22	
    23	### Audience
    24	
    25	If you are running more than one slurm job at a time, you should try
    26	`reportseff`.  Users of HPC systems can get an idea how well they estimate
    27	resource usage.  By tuning these values, you can get scheduled earlier and not
    28	be penalized for unused allocations.  Since `reportseff` can parse job ids from
    29	slurm output files, it simplifies the task of identifying which jobs have
    30	failed and why. Sys admins can pipe `reportseff` output to identify users with
    31	poor utilization or produce summaries at the end of a billing cycle.
    32	
    33	### Implementation
    34	
    35	`reportseff` is a wrapper around `sacct` that provides more complex option
    36	parsing, simpler options, and cleaner, colored outputs.  All querying is
    37	performed in a single call to `sacct` and should have similar performance.
    38	Multi-node and GPU utilization is acquired from information contained in the
    39	`AdminComment` field, as generated by `jobstats`.
    40	
    41	## Usage
    42	
    43	### Installation
    44	
    45	`reportseff` runs on python >= 3.6.
    46	The only external dependency is click (>= 6.7).
    47	Calling
    48	
    49	```sh
    50	pip install --user reportseff
    51	# OR
    52	pipx install reportseff
    53	```
    54	
    55	will create command line bindings and install click.
    56	
    57	### Sample Usage
    58	
    59	Try `reportseff -u $USER` or just `reportseff` in a directory with some slurm
    60	outputs.  You may be surprised by your results!
    61	
    62	#### Single job
    63	
    64	Calling `reportseff` with a single jobid will provide equivalent information to
    65	seff for that job. `reportseff 24371789` and `reportseff map_fastq_24371789`
    66	produce the following output:
    67	
    68	```txt
    69	   JobID      State          Elapsed   CPUEff   MemEff
    70	24371789    COMPLETED       03:08:03   71.2%    45.7%
    71	```
    72	
    73	#### Single array job
    74	
    75	Providing either the raw job id or the array job id will get efficiency
    76	information for a single element of the array job. `reportseff 24220929_421`
    77	and `reportseff 24221219` generate:
    78	
    79	```txt
    80	       JobID      State          Elapsed    CPUEff   MemEff
    81	24220929_421    COMPLETED       00:09:34    99.0%    34.6%
    82	```
    83	
    84	#### Array job group
    85	
    86	If the base job id of an array is provided, all elements of the array will
    87	be added to the output. `reportseff 24220929`
    88	
    89	```txt
    90	          JobID      State          Elapsed    CPUEff   MemEff
    91	     24220929_1    COMPLETED       00:10:43    99.2%    33.4%
    92	    24220929_11    COMPLETED       00:10:10    99.2%    37.5%
    93	    24220929_21    COMPLETED       00:09:25    98.8%    36.1%
    94	    24220929_31    COMPLETED       00:09:19    98.9%    33.3%
    95	    24220929_41    COMPLETED       00:09:23    98.9%    33.3%
    96	    24220929_51    COMPLETED       00:08:02    98.5%    36.3%

   141	#### Filtering slurm output files
   142	
   143	One useful application of `reportseff` is filtering a directory of slurm output
   144	files based on the state or time since running. Additionally, if only the
   145	`jobid` is specified as a format output, the filenames will be returned in a
   146	pipe-friendly manner:
   147	
   148	```txt
   149	old_runs   ❯❯❯ reportseff --since d=4 --state Timeout
   150	
   151	                 JobID   State      Elapsed  CPUEff   MemEff
   152	call_variants_31550458  TIMEOUT    20:05:17  99.5%     0.0%
   153	call_variants_31550474  TIMEOUT    20:05:17  99.6%     0.0%
   154	call_variants_31550500  TIMEOUT    20:05:08  99.7%     0.0%
   155	old_runs   ❯❯❯ reportseff --since d=4 --state Timeout --format jobid
   156	call_variants_31550458
   157	call_variants_31550474
   158	call_variants_31550500
   159	```
   160	
   161	To find all lines with `output:` in jobs which have timed out or failed
   162	in the last 4 days:
   163	
   164	```sh
   165	reportseff --since 'd=4' --state TO,F --format jobid | xargs grep output:
   166	```
   167	
   168	### Arguments
   169	
   170	Jobs can be passed as arguments in the following ways:
   171	
   172	- Job ID such as 1234567.  If the id is part of an array job, only the element
   173	for that ID will be displayed.  If the id is the base part of an array job,
   174	all elements in the array will be displayed.
   175	- Array Job ID such as 1234567\_89.  Will display only the element specified.
   176	- Slurm output file.  Format must be BASE\_%A\_%a.  BASE is optional as is a
   177	'.out' suffix.  Unix glob expansions can also be used to filter which jobs
   178	are displayed.
   179	- From current directory.  If no argument is supplied, `reportseff` will attempt
   180	to find slurm output files in the current directory as described above.
   181	If a user is provided, instead `reportseff` will show recent jobs for that user.
   182	If only `since` is set, all recent jobs for all users will be shown (if allowed).
   183	- Supplying a directory as a single argument will override the current
   184	directory to check for slurm outputs.
   185	
   186	### Options
   187	
   188	- `--color/--no-color`: Force color output or not.  By default, will force color
   189	  output.  With the no-color flag, click will strip color codes for everything
   190	  besides stdout.
   191	- `--modified-sort`: Instead of sorting by filename/jobid, sort by last
   192	  modification time of the slurm output file.
   193	- `--debug`: Write sacct result to stderr.
   194	- `--user/-u`: Ignore job arguments and instead query sacct with provided user.
   195	  Returns all jobs from the last week.
   196	- `--state/-s`: Output only jobs with states matching one of the provided options.
   197	  Accepts comma separated values of job codes (e.g. 'R') or full names
   198	  (e.g. RUNNING).  Case insensitive.
   199	- `--not-state/-S`: Output only jobs with states not matching any of the provided options.
   200	  Accepts comma separated values of job codes (e.g. 'R') or full names
   201	  (e.g. RUNNING).  Case insensitive.
   202	- `--format`: Provide a comma separated list of columns to produce. Prefixing the
   203	  argument with `+` adds the specified values to the defaults.  Values can
   204	  be any valid column name to sacct and the custom efficiency values: TimeEff,
   205	  cpuEff, MemEff.  Can also optionally set alignment (<, ^, >) and maximum width.
   206	  Default is center-aligned with a width of the maximum column entry.  For
   207	  example, `--format 'jobid%>,state%10,memeff%<5'` produces 3 columns with:
   208	  - JobId aligned right, width set automatically
   209	  - State with width 10 (center aligned by default)
   210	  - MemEff aligned left, width 5
   211	- `--slurm-format`: The filename pattern passed to sbatch during job submission.
   212	  Overrides the default regex for job id parsing from filenames.  E.g. to match
   213	  filenames like `123456.out` set `--slurm-format %j.out`.
   214	- `--since`: Limit results to those occurring after the specified time.  Accepts
   215	  sacct formats and a comma separated list of key/value pairs.  To get jobs in
   216	  the last hour and a half, can pass `h=1,m=30`.
   217	- `--node/-n`: Display information for multi-node jobs; requires additional
   218	  sacct fields from jobstats.
   219	- `--node-and-gpu/-g`: Display information for multi-node jobs and GPU information;
   220	  requires additional sacct fields from jobstats.
   221	- `--parsable/-p`: Ignore formatting and output as a `|` delimited table.  Useful
   222	  for piping into more complex analyses.
   223

   241	## Troubleshooting
   242	
   243	### I can't install, what is pip?
   244	
   245	[pip](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/) is the package installer for python.  If
   246	you get an error that pip isn't found, look for a python/anaconda/conda module.
   247	[pipx](https://pypa.github.io/pipx/) ensures that each application is installed
   248	in an isolated environment.  This resolves issues of dependency versions and
   249	allows applications to be run from any environment.
   250	
   251	### I get an error about broken pipes when chaining to other commands
   252	
   253	Python will report that the consumer of process output has closed the stream
   254	(i.e. the pipe) while still attempting to write.  Newer versions of click
   255	should suppress the warning output, but it seems to not always work.  Besides
   256	some extra printing on stderr, the output is not affected.
   257	
   258	### My jobs don't have any information about multiple nodes or GPU efficiency
   259	
   260	Because `sacct` doesn't currently record this information, `reportseff`
   261	retrieves it from a custom field from `jobstats`, developed at Princeton
   262	University.  If you are outside a Research Computing cluster, that information
   263	will likely be absent.  Node-level reporting is only shown for jobs which use
   264	multiple nodes or GPUs.  If you need a list of where jobs were run, you can add
   265	`--format +NodeList`.
   266	
   267	### My output is garbled with ESC[0m all over, where's the color?
   268	
   269	Those are ANSI color codes.  Click will usually strip these if it detects
   270	the consuming process can't display color codes, but `reportseff` defaults
   271	to always display them.  If you don't care for color, use the `--no-color`
   272	option.  For less, you can set
   273	```
   274	export LESS="-R"
   275	```
   276	in your `.bashrc`, or just type `-R` in an active less process.  Some versions
   277	of `watch` require the `-c` option to display color, others can't display
   278	colors properly.  If you search for `ansi color <tool>` you should get some
   279	solutions.
